notes:
- Comments and title pages no longer close the app: Opening a comment thread or an anime's page could force-stop when the network layer threw instead of answering with a failure, when a title page drew a row with a repeated list key, or when a theme colour could not be saved while the sheet opened. Those now surface where they belong: the comment sheet's own error row with Try again, the broken-heart status, or the summary the title page was already showing. A synopsis or comment with malformed markup is drawn as plain text rather than taking its screen down with it, and a failed title fetch leaves the page usable and able to try again.
- The AniList check says when the check itself failed: A reachability check from Settings that throws instead of answering used to look exactly like one that was still running. It now shows a toast with the bad news, keeps the dialog open, and leaves Check again ready - and a retry that fails the same way says so again rather than going quiet.
- The board can be narrowed by genre and by studio: The filter sheet now lists every genre on your list, and has a Studio section that is off until you switch it on. Studios are sorted by how many titles in your library each one made, so the ones you watch most come first. Opening the section and selecting nothing shows every studio; selections are kept while the section is off, so flipping it back on restores them rather than silently forgetting. The board and the unranked shelf use the same filters, and the sheet scrolls when a long studio list would otherwise run off the bottom.
- The whole tier list exports as one image: Export from the board's floating toolbar, then share the PNG or save it to Pictures/AniSequel. It renders every tier and every ranked poster at a fixed 1080-unit width - a single image rather than a screenshot of whatever fits on screen - and keeps the current genre and studio filters. Missing posters fall back to a filled tile instead of failing the export, and very large boards are scaled to stay within a safe bitmap size.
- Zoom goes down to 35%, and the board can be locked: The zoom range is 35-200% now, enough to see a few hundred titles on one screen. A magnifier in the app bar opens a zoom sheet with a slider and presets, the bottom stepper is smaller, and tapping its percentage resets to 100%. The lock toggle - in the stepper and the zoom sheet - turns off long-press tile dragging so a pinch is no longer taken by the drag gesture. Captions and score badges disappear below 60% instead of overflowing their tiles, and tier labels shrink to fit the narrower gutter.
- A calmer top bar and safer empty states: The Tiers action is an icon now, which gives the list's own name room on a 360dp screen. Titles whose cached list entry predates the genre and studio fields, posters that fail to load, and a list with no studio credits all render as empty sections or placeholder tiles instead of a null lookup. The filter and zoom sheets bound their height and scroll, so a long list of options cannot push the close action off the display.
